correctness.rationale: The graph and synchronous rule are exactly defined. Walsh eigenvalues \(5^1,1^{10},(-3)^5\) give A-I nullity 10; each force preserves vanishing of a kernel vector and yields an unconditional \(Z\ge10\). The explicit 10-set forces six whites in two rounds, hence \(Z=M=10\). Separate C++ bitmask and Python set-based implementations each examine all 65,536 subsets, verify coefficients 3872,3632,1760,560,120,16,1, prove inclusion-minimal sets only have size10 and every minimum set takes two synchronous rounds. The 1920 automorphisms are proved full using generator-neighbor pair rigidity. All 8008 six-white complements are partitioned into 18 group orbits, seven forcing, with sizes 960,960,480,480,480,320,192. The embedded checker validates every CSV row. No inference from partial sampling or computational timeout is used.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The general inequality relating maximum nullity and zero-forcing number is sufficient for a LOWER bound and is already credited, but cannot determine 3,872 forcing sets, their symmetry orbits, or their round times. Polynomial calculations for trees, complete multipartite, wheels and other special families do not include this primitive strongly regular graph. A universal closed formula specialized to this graph was not located. Directly inspected 2012 Table 1 discusses the complete nontrivial powers of the Clebsch graph, not the degree-five base object.

value.rationale: This primitive 16-vertex 5-regular strongly regular Cayley graph is a canonical test object for forcing and symmetry. A complete forcing polynomial, an equality of zero forcing and nullity, seven inequivalent minimum configurations, nontrivial well-forcedness beyond tree families and uniform two-round propagation provide a coherent structural classification, useful as a precise finite benchmark. The claim does not rely only on a small numerical improvement or relabeling.
